readings.title: A Sunny Day in the Forest
readings.passage: Linh and her family went camping in Ba Vi National Park last weekend. The forest was green and peaceful, filled with the singing of wild birds. In the morning, they walked along a pine trail and discovered a sparkling mountain stream. They had a delicious picnic with sandwiches and fruit under a shady oak tree. It was an unforgettable adventure close to nature.
readings.vietnameseTranslation: Linh và gia đình đã đi cắm trại ở Vườn quốc gia Ba Vì vào cuối tuần trước. Khu rừng xanh mướt và yên bình, ngập tràn tiếng chim hót hoang dã. Vào buổi sáng, họ đi dạo dọc theo con đường mòn thông và phát hiện một dòng suối núi lấp lánh. Họ đã có một bữa dã ngoại ngon miệng với bánh mì kẹp và trái cây dưới bóng râm cây sồi. Đó là một chuyến phiêu lưu khó quên gần gũi với thiên nhiên.

readings.title: My Friendly Puppy Max
readings.passage: Max is a friendly golden puppy. He has big floppy ears and a wagging tail. Every afternoon, Max plays catch with a bright tennis ball in our backyard. When he gets tired, he drinks cool water and takes a nap on his soft blanket. Everyone in our neighborhood smiles when they see Max.
readings.vietnameseTranslation: Max là một chú cún con lông vàng thân thiện. Chú có đôi tai to mềm rủ và chiếc đuôi luôn vẫy mừng. Mỗi buổi chiều, Max chơi ném bắt bóng với quả bóng tennis sáng màu ở sân sau. Khi mệt, chú uống nước mát và ngủ trưa trên tấm chăn êm ái. Mọi người trong khu phố đều mỉm cười khi nhìn thấy Max.

questions.explanation: The passage clearly introduces Max as a friendly golden puppy.

questions.explanation: Max plays catch with a bright tennis ball in the backyard.

readings.title: The Power of Daily Habits
readings.passage: Success is rarely the result of a single monumental breakthrough. Instead, it stems from the small, consistent habits we practice every day. Reading ten pages of an English book each morning or practicing five vocabulary flashcards during a commute may seem minor, but over months these micro-habits compound into extraordinary fluency and confidence.
readings.vietnameseTranslation: Thành công hiếm khi là kết quả của một bước đột phá kỳ vĩ đơn lẻ. Thay vào đó, nó bắt nguồn từ những thói quen nhỏ, kiên trì mà chúng ta rèn luyện mỗi ngày. Đọc mười trang sách tiếng Anh mỗi sáng hoặc luyện năm thẻ từ vựng trên đường đi học có vẻ nhỏ nhặt, nhưng sau nhiều tháng, những vi thói quen này sẽ cộng dồn thành sự trôi chảy và tự tin phi thường.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the main driver of long-term success?

questions.explanation: The passage explains that success stems from small, consistent daily habits.

questions.question: What happens when micro-habits are practiced over months?
options: They take too much time to sustain
questions.explanation: Over months, these micro-habits compound into extraordinary fluency and confidence.

grammar.incorrectSentence: He go to the bookstore every Sunday morning.
grammar.correctSentence: He goes to the bookstore every Sunday morning.
grammar.ruleExplanation: With third-person singular subjects (he, she, it), the present simple verb must add -s or -es.
grammar.hint: Check the subject 'He' and match the verb form for present simple.

grammar.incorrectSentence: The students in our class is very enthusiastic.
grammar.correctSentence: The students in our class are very enthusiastic.
grammar.ruleExplanation: The true subject is plural ('The students'), so use the plural verb 'are' instead of 'is'.
grammar.hint: Look past prepositional phrases like 'in our class' to find the real plural subject.

grammar.incorrectSentence: She don't like drinking bitter coffee without sugar.
grammar.correctSentence: She doesn't like drinking bitter coffee without sugar.
grammar.ruleExplanation: Use 'doesn't' (does not) for third-person singular subjects (he/she/it).
grammar.hint: The negative auxiliary verb for 'She' in the present tense is 'doesn't'.

grammar.incorrectSentence: Everyone in the room were looking forward to the speech.
grammar.correctSentence: Everyone in the room was looking forward to the speech.
grammar.ruleExplanation: Indefinite pronouns such as 'everyone', 'everybody', and 'someone' take a singular verb.
grammar.hint: 'Everyone' refers to individuals singularly, so use 'was'.

grammar.incorrectSentence: Yesterday she buy a new digital camera at the mall.
grammar.correctSentence: Yesterday she bought a new digital camera at the mall.
grammar.ruleExplanation: Use past simple ('bought') when referring to a completed action in the past ('yesterday').
grammar.hint: The time signal 'Yesterday' requires the irregular past tense of 'buy'.

grammar.incorrectSentence: I have visited Da Nang city three years ago.
grammar.correctSentence: I visited Da Nang city three years ago.
grammar.ruleExplanation: When a specific past time is given ('three years ago'), use the simple past tense, not present perfect.
grammar.hint: Specific time markers like 'ago' require simple past.

grammar.incorrectSentence: She has been living in Hanoi since five years.
grammar.correctSentence: She has been living in Hanoi for five years.
grammar.ruleExplanation: Use 'for' with a duration of time ('five years') and 'since' with a specific starting point in time.
grammar.hint: 'Five years' is a duration, so use 'for'.

grammar.incorrectSentence: He wants to become an software engineer in the future.
grammar.correctSentence: He wants to become a software engineer in the future.
grammar.ruleExplanation: Use 'a' before words starting with a consonant sound ('software' begins with /s/).
grammar.hint: Check whether the next word begins with a vowel sound or consonant sound.

grammar.incorrectSentence: She ate a apple after finishing her lunch.
grammar.correctSentence: She ate an apple after finishing her lunch.
grammar.ruleExplanation: Use 'an' before words beginning with a vowel sound (/æ/ in 'apple').
grammar.hint: Apple begins with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.

grammar.incorrectSentence: The concert will begin in 7:00 PM tonight.
grammar.correctSentence: The concert will begin at 7:00 PM tonight.
grammar.ruleExplanation: Use the preposition 'at' for specific times of the day (e.g., at 7:00 PM).
grammar.hint: Preposition for specific clock times is 'at'.

grammar.ruleExplanation: Use 'in' for months, years, and seasons without a specific day.
grammar.hint: When naming only the month without a date, use 'in'.
